name: POLIGNAC
description: Polignac is a French reverse trick-taking game in which players try to avoid taking Jacks, especially the Jack of Spades, the Polignac.

content.text: Polignac is a French reverse trick-taking game in which players try to avoid taking Jacks, especially the Jack of Spades, the Polignac.
Dates back to the early 19th century in France. It is named after the French Prime Minister Jules de Polignac, who was deeply unpopular at the timeâ€”hence why the most 'Penalty' card bears his name.
4 is standard; 5 or 6 requires removing specific cards (like 7s) to make dealing even.

items.text: Capot: Before the opening lead, a player may bid capot: an undertaking to win every trick. If they succeed, each opponent loses 5 points; if they fail, the bidder loses 5.

General: A player may announce before leading to the first trick that they will try to take all tricks. Success: all other players score 5 penalty points each. Failure: Jacks score 5 points in the usual way against the players who take them.
Ace high variant: If Ace is played as high (common in old French games), penalties attach to Queens instead of Jacks.
